ui.param.fw.confirm_txt:
The wing's firmware belongs to MA Lighting — Wing Bridge can't provide it. The only way to get it: listen to grandMA2 onPC while it sends it to the wing itself. So you need grandMA2 onPC installed and launchable on this PC (just for this operation — you won't need it afterward). Windows x64 only — not Windows ARM: USBPcap and grandMA2 onPC only exist for x64.

To do this, Wing Bridge temporarily installs USBPcap (an open-source USB capture component), records the firmware once, then uninstalls it. A Windows prompt will ask for permission.

You'll be guided step by step (7 steps), each one unlocking on its own: launch grandMA2 onPC → unplug the wing → (installation) → plug in the wing → close grandMA2 onPC → unplug the wing (USBPcap removal) → plug the wing back in → Wing Bridge takes over. Allow 2 to 4 minutes, and during that time the wing will power off/on several times — that's normal, don't plug or unplug anything until the assistant asks you to.

ui.faders.hrangee.body:
In grandMA3, every page has the same layout: one row 101→110, another 201→210, and so on. And an executor number is always relative to the current page — Executor 206 means the 206 of the page shown.

As a result, you only fill in the row once, and changing pages follows automatically. Nothing else to touch.

The label to the left of each fader is there to match your wing's screen printing (Master, XFade, 1, 2…). It changes nothing about what's sent: it's just so you can find your way around, since MA2 command wings don't all have the same number of faders or the same layout.
ui.encodeurs.hattr.body:
The name to enter here is the attribute's internal MA3 name, not the label shown on the Encoder Bar. The two look similar enough to trip you up:
  • Encoder Bar “Focus” → write Focus1
  • Encoder Bar “Sh1” → write Shutter1
  • Encoder Bar “Dim” → write Dimmer
  • Encoder Bar “P” / “T” → write Pan / Tilt
A name that doesn't exist fails silently: Wing Bridge sends the command with no error, and it's MA3 that refuses it — on its command line, with illegal object. Nothing shows up in the app's log. If a wheel seems dead, check MA3's command line.

You don't have to guess: the full list is right below, and the fields suggest names as you type.
ui.param.gma3.hplugin.body:
1. Copy the files onto every machine running MA3 (importing a show doesn't copy them):
  • macOS — run plugin_ma3/installer.sh: it copies the files into ~/MALightingTechnology/gma3_library/datapools/plugins/ and checks the Lua syntax along the way.
  • Windows — copy wingbridge.lua, wingbridge.xml, wingloader.lua and wingloader.xml (the plugin_ma3 folder) to C:\ProgramData\MALightingTechnology\gma3_library\datapools\plugins\.
2. In grandMA3, one command after another (location {slot} — configurable in Settings → 🎛️ grandMA3):
  Import Plugin Library "wingloader.xml" At {slot}
  Set Plugin {slot}.1 Property "Installed" "Yes"
  Plugin {slot}
  (if MA3 offers Overwrite / Merge / Cancel — slot {slot} already taken — choose Overwrite.)
3. Save the show: the plugin's location is part of the showfile; without saving it disappears when MA3 restarts (the files on disk stay put).
Once the loader is imported, any new version of the probe is picked up on the next Plugin {slot} — no re-import or MA3 restart needed.
ui.param.gma3.hactiver.body:

⚠️ Menu → Network: the button at the bottom right must be green — global network off means no sockets, OSC included.

grandMA3 sends sACN or Art-Net → the wing outputs the universe on its DMX XLR.
In MA3: Menu → In & Out → DMX Protocols → enable sACN (or Art-Net), with the wanted output universe.

ui.param.scan.hlire.body:
• Supported: known VID:PID (0x03EB:0x160B) — works out of the box.
• Candidate: Atmel chip or endpoints identical to the known wing — Test the handshake to check it speaks the same protocol.
• A device that responds to the handshake like the known wing → very likely the same PCB → compatible.
• A different VID:PID that doesn't respond → different chip: its USB protocol needs to be captured to add it. Copy the report and keep it.
ui.param.fw.hrepli.body: On a Windows x64 PC: install Wireshark (it offers USBPcap), start capturing on the USBPcapN interface of the hub the wing will be on, plug in the wing / open grandMA2 onPC (the upload takes ~2-3 s), stop and save as .pcapng. Import that file below: if the fingerprint matches, you're good. On a Mac (or any machine that isn't the one you captured on): capture once on a Windows PC using the button above, “💾 Export the firmware” once it's cached, copy the .bin, then “📄 Import a firmware (.bin)” here. Details: docs/HARDWARE.md.
ui.bridge.intro:
Wing Bridge Bridges a grandMA2 Command Wing and grandMA3: keys, faders and encoders drive MA3 like a real command section.
Two channels need setting up, both of them: OSC for commands, and a plugin installed in MA3 that reports console state back (executor LEDs, current page, fader catch-up). A virtual keyboard completes the picture for MA3's command line (console mode). Everything is configured in the Settings tab.
ui.touches.intro:
🔘 Keys — assign the buttons Decide what each button on the wing does. Click Learning mode, press a physical button, and give it an MA3 command (e.g. Store, Fixture). For an executor, choose 2-role Executor then the Function actually assigned to that executor in MA3 — Go+, Toggle, Flash, Swap… (Go+ isn't the only syntax, unlike what the app used to do: each executor can have its own function). Flash / Temp / Swap are held (active as long as the button stays pressed, cut on release) — the others are single hits. Assignments are saved to the current profile.

Double-press: an extra MA3 command, sent on two quick presses of the same key (e.g. Menu ×2 → SaveShow). ⚠️ This field expects a full MA3 keyword (“SaveShow”, “Highlight”, “Hi”…), not a keystroke — unlike the “Keyboard shortcut” column right next to it, which expects a key (“H”, “F5”…).
ui.faders.intro:
🎚️ Faders — to MA3 masters For each physical fader, choose the type to drive — modeled on the Select Function list MA3 offers for an executor's Fader property (Executor menu → Fader). The list of types is detailed further down, with the exact command sent.
⚠️ The type chosen here MUST match the function actually set on that executor in MA3 (Executor menu → Fader → Select Function, or Set Page X.N Property "Fader" <Function>). OSC doesn't see what you configured on MA3's side — it's the command that's sent that decides, so both settings must match.
Tip: enable learning mode and move a fader to spot its byte number.
ui.encodeurs.intro: 🎡 Encoders — the 4 wheels Each wheel controls an attribute of the fixtures selected in MA3 (Dimmer, Pan, Tilt, color…). A click on a wheel reassigns all 4 wheels at once (like an attribute group); a double-click activates a second set — 8 groups in total, configured here the same way.
ui.profils.intro: 💾 Profiles — save your settings A profile groups together all your mappings (keys, faders, wheels, LEDs, console shortcuts). Save it under a name, and if you have several wings, load the right profile for each one.

aide.demarrage.html:
Four things to check. The first three are in grandMA3, the last one in this app. As long as one is missing, some keys will stay silent — with no error message.

1 · OSC: where the commands travel

MA3 → Menu → In & Out → OSC

  • Interface: the Mac's network interface (e.g. en0) — never <None>. ⚠️ This setting sometimes resets when a show loads: it's the first thing to recheck if nothing responds anymore.
  • Enable Input: on — mandatory, it's what receives the wing's commands.
  • ONLY ONE line matters: the one whose Port is 8000 — the port the app sends to. Set it like this: Destination IP 127.0.0.1 if MA3 runs on this Mac, otherwise this machine's IP · Mode UDP · Prefix empty · Receive Yes · Receive Command Yes — this is what EXECUTES the commands, without it MA3 receives and ignores them · Fader Range 100.
  • The other lines don't get in the way. MA3 often shows several, one per use — that's normal. An OUTPUT line (MA3 → app, typically port 8001, Send set to Yes) doesn't need Receive Command, and Wing Bridge doesn't require it: the app doesn't listen for OSC. What comes back from the console goes through the plugin, not OSC.
  • MA3 on another machine? Put its IP in the Settings tab. It's specific to this Mac: it doesn't travel with the profiles you exchange.

⚠️ The app's diagnostic only checks the port 8000 line. If it flags an OSC problem, that's the one it's talking about — not the others.

⚠️ If MA3 refuses to open the port even though the config is correct, check Menu → Network: the button at the bottom right must be GREEN. On a red background, MA3's global network is off and no socket opens, OSC included.

2 · Keyboard shortcuts: the same on both sides

Some keys go through the keyboard, not OSC. So the app and MA3 must agree on which keystroke does what. Tab Keys → Send the shortcuts to MA3. The app writes its table into MA3 and tells you what the console actually accepted.

3 · Enable the shortcuts in MA3

In MA3, the shortcut table must be active (KeyboardShortcutsActive). The send above turns it on by itself — but if you switch user profile in MA3, check again.

4 · The “wingbridge” plugin in MA3

It's what reports the console's state back: current page, executors, actual fader position. Without it, the app still works, but it goes blind — no fader catch-up, no LED reflecting MA3, no configuration following.

Install it, then launch it from MA3. The MA3 probe pill at the top turns green as soon as it talks.

Once these four points are in place, all that's left is to plug in the wing and click Start. The USB connection re-establishes itself if you unplug and replug.
aide.suivreMa3.html:
On a real command wing, the physical fader does what the executor says — not what's configured elsewhere. Checked, Wing Bridge behaves the same way: it's MA3 that has the final say.

  • An executor set to Flash in MA3 will do a Flash, even if your profile says Go+.
  • An empty slot receives nothing — just like on a console, where pushing a fader across from a gap does nothing.
  • A function the app can't send is not guessed: nothing goes out, and the log says so.

As long as the MA3 plugin isn't installed (Settings tab → grandMA3), this setting has nothing to follow and has no effect. Unchecked, Wing Bridge strictly obeys your profile.
aide.suivreEncMa3.html:
On a real command wing, the wheels do what the Encoder Bar shows for the selected fixture. Checked, Wing Bridge behaves the same way: the 4 wheels reflect the actual attributes of the 1st fixture in MA3's selection, whatever its type (color, position, gobo, beam…).

  • Known limitation, not a bug: on a mixed selection (RGB + CMY together, for example), the wheels follow the first selected fixture, not an average or a merge of the two.
  • No fixture selected in MA3 → the wheels send nothing — just like on a console, turning a wheel over an empty programmer does nothing.
  • A fixture with fewer than 4 attributes → the extra wheels send nothing either.

As long as the MA3 plugin isn't installed (Settings tab → grandMA3), this setting has no effect. Unchecked (the default setting), the wheels keep the attribute groups configured below.
aide.faderPickup.html:
After a page change or a show reload, the physical fader and MA3's value are no longer in the same place. On first contact, the level jumps — and that shows from the house.

With catch-up, a fader only takes control once it has reached MA3's value, exactly like on a real console. The concerned executor's LED flashes as long as it isn't caught up: you can see where the mismatch is without looking at the screen.

As long as the MA3 plugin isn't installed, no effect — the app can't know where the console's faders stand.
aide.ledMa3.html:
Executor button LEDs take on the console's actual state: full brightness when the sequence is running, half-level when something is loaded but stopped, dimmed when the slot is empty.

This was one of the most visible gaps before the plugin: the LEDs said nothing about what was happening on the console.

As long as the MA3 plugin isn't installed, all LEDs stay dimmed. Pressing still lights the key under your finger.
aide.verbeCible.html:
Just like on a console: you type Store, then press an executor button — and the command goes out complete, Store Executor 105.

It works with Store, Update, Delete, Copy, Move, Assign, Edit, Label, Goto, Select, Off, On, Kill, Toggle… Verbs with two targets (Copy, Move) expect the source then the destination.

Unchecked, pressing an executor always keeps its direct action, even after a Store. Useful if you'd rather drive the command line entirely from MA3.
aide.usbArrache.html:
There's nothing to do. Plug it back in: the app finds the wing on its own and restarts the bridge if it was running.

If the wing comes back “slow” (it happens), the app detects it and fixes it in under a second, without asking you anything.

The only case that needs a gesture: the wing comes back in bootloader. The USB Wing pill says so plainly then, and the only fix is to cut its power — unplug then replug the cable. A software reset isn't enough.
aide.raccourcis.html:
Some of the wing's keys don't reach MA3 via OSC but via the keyboard — it's the only way to write into the real command line, and so to make Store + click on a preset work like on a console.

For that, the app and MA3 must hold the same table. The button writes the app's into MA3 and applies it, then reads back what the console actually accepted — it doesn't just read back its own file.

What it doesn't do

  • It doesn't overwrite everything. The app knows 49 of MA3's 82 keys; the others (numpad, X keys, onPC screens) are copied as-is.
  • It doesn't send if it's already in place. Nothing is written or sent when MA3's table already matches.
  • It refuses on collision. If a keystroke is already another MA3 key's, the send is blocked and it tells you — otherwise the console would trigger the other function and you'd think the wing was broken.

⭐ The golden rule for filling in the fields

Write exactly what MA3's shortcut table shows. MA3 shows “Alt+A” → write Alt+A. MA3 shows “Ctrl+Alt+semicolon” → write Ctrl+Alt+semicolon.

MA3 labels keys in US positions: on an AZERTY keyboard, your M key shows as “semicolon”. That's normal — copy it as-is.

Accepted syntax: a letter or digit (s, 5), a key name (Enter, F5, semicolon, comma, period…), or a combination with +.

A keyword coming out wrong? Write it in quotes so it's typed out in full: "If" instead of i. MA3 autocompletes what you type, and a single letter can be ambiguous — i can give IfOutput instead of If.
aide.accessibilite.html:
macOS forbids an app from sending keystrokes without explicit permission. Without it, keys can't reach MA3 — the app then falls back to OSC only, with fewer functions.

Click 🔓 Allow Accessibility. The button does everything: it clears old, stale authorizations, restarts the assistant, and opens the right Settings pane.

You should see a single “Wing Keyboard” line — check it. The Keyboard pill turns green on its own within ~3 seconds: don't click anything else.

If it stays red

Check that the box is really checked (not just present), then click 🔄 Reset at the top. If several “Wing Keyboard” lines appear, uncheck them all, click 🔓 again, and check the only one that remains.

⚠️ After an app update, the authorization resets. That's normal: the app isn't signed with a paid Apple certificate, so macOS sees it as a new app. Redo 🔓.
aide.conflitRaccourci.titre: A button triggers something else in MA3
aide.conflitRaccourci.html:
This is a keyboard shortcut conflict on MA3's side: the keystroke is already used elsewhere — for example Alt+A means “Camera Set Pivot” in a 3D view, not Assign. The app does send the right key, it's MA3 that redirects it.

Diagnosis

Look at MA3's command line history: it shows the command actually triggered.

Fix

In MA3, reassign that command to a free shortcut — the F9 to F20 keys are ideal, rarely in conflict. Then copy MA3's exact label into the matching field in the Keys tab.

Tip for recording an F key in MA3: macOS intercepts F9-F12 (volume, brightness). Open the assignment window in MA3, then send the key from the 🧪 field alongside — MA3 will capture it cleanly.
aide.plugin.titre: Install the MA3 plugin — console state feedback
aide.plugin.html:
The plugin is a required install step, just like configuring the firmware. Without it, Wing Bridge sends OSC blind: button LEDs don't reflect MA3's state, there's no fader catch-up (pickup) after a page change, and the app doesn't know the current page. The app doesn't crash without the plugin — it runs in a degraded mode, which isn't the goal.

It's a small Lua probe that runs INSIDE MA3 and writes its state to a file once a second — the only feedback channel, OSC only goes one way.

The simplest way: automatic installation

With grandMA3 running, go to Settings → 🧩 Wing firmware and click “🧩 Install automatically”. The app copies the files into MA3's pool, sends the import + SaveShow, and checks that the probe responds. If it fails (MA3 not listening for OSC, the slot already taken…), follow the manual procedure below.

⚠️ Importing a show does NOT install the plugin

A showfile contains the plugin's entry in the pool, but not the files. The files must be copied onto every machine (step 1), once and for all. Otherwise MA3 shows the plugin but Plugin (at your location) loads nothing.

Windows

  1. Copy the 4 files wingbridge.lua, wingbridge.xml, wingloader.lua and wingloader.xml from Wing Bridge's plugin_ma3 folder to MA3's plugins folder:
    C:\ProgramData\MALightingTechnology\gma3_library\datapools\plugins\
    (on Windows that's ProgramData, not your user folder).
  2. 3 below is the default location — configurable in Settings → 🎛️ grandMA3 (“Plugin location”) if that slot is already taken by another plugin; replace 3 with your slot in the three commands then. In MA3, type these three commands:
    • Import Plugin Library "wingloader.xml" At 3
    • Set Plugin 3.1 Property "Installed" "Yes"
    • Plugin 3
    If MA3 offers Overwrite / Merge / Cancel (the slot is already taken, e.g. by an imported show), choose Overwrite.
  3. Save the show — the plugin's location is part of the showfile; without saving it disappears when MA3 restarts (the files on disk stay put).
  4. Check: the MA3 probe pill at the top turns green.

macOS

  1. Run plugin_ma3/installer.sh: it copies the files into ~/MALightingTechnology/gma3_library/datapools/plugins/ and checks the Lua syntax along the way.
  2. The same three commands in MA3: Import Plugin Library "wingloader.xml" At 3, Set Plugin 3.1 Property "Installed" "Yes", Plugin 3.
  3. Save the show.

These three commands also go through OSC, so remotely too. Once the loader is imported, any new version of the probe is picked up on the next Plugin (by name, or by your location) — no re-import or MA3 restart needed.

err.desinstall.plugin_ma3: In grandMA3: remove the plugin from the pool (Edit Plugin → Wing Loader slot). The keyboard shortcut table Wing Bridge wrote into MA3 stays — reset it by hand if needed.

err.desinstall.corbeille_windows: Move the app folder to the Trash: dist-windows\.
